system.summary: French homophonic cipher of the 1560s for German affairs (Tomokiyo's reconstructed table): two to four signs per letter, a few code words and nulls.

diacritics.note: Crossed and barred strokes distinguish signs (four cross shapes, ⊢ = q, ⊣ = r, + = o); the looped y-shape serves both s and p in the contributed reading.

system.doubled_letters: eight doubled-letter signs (ee ff ii ll mm nn rr ss), and pp = ff
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo, Cryptiana frencheastern.htm, 'French Ciphers for German (and Eastern) Affairs': key reconstructed for this volume.
system.notes: All 44 pages are in one key (one-key rule checked from the contributed key.tsv: one table, inferred values added). contributed/data/key.tsv has 95 entries (72 from Tomokiyo's table, 23 inferred): 12 word codes, 8 doubled-letter signs, 20 named null groups. Sign names are the contributor's; key in contributed/data/key.tsv.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo published the reconstructed key for this volume (Cryptiana frencheastern.htm) but no reading of the passages; the volume holds one contemporary decipherment (view 23 right) of the 15 Nov 1567 letter. Contributor's prior-work check found no earlier reading.

conditions.human_role: Contributed result: Harumi-Matsuba's account (created 19 Oct 2026) reports that a person chose the target and decided to publish; transcription, decoding and checks were by Claude and OpenAI Codex. In this project the result was checked by Claude (Opus 5.5) at Daniel Bourdeau's request.

solution.what: Contributor took Tomokiyo's reconstructed table (Cryptiana frencheastern.htm) as the key and named its signs (key.tsv); values for signs not in the table and nulls inferred from context (16 = ce, ꝭs = t, ρ = e, ꝑꝑ = ff).

Contributor: Claude transcribed 44 pages (822 lines, 29,707 signs) from BnF IIIF line crops; disagreements with Codex runs checked on enlarged crops by Codex and Claude Sonnet, corrected only where both agreed.

Contributor: 1000 shuffled keys per page scored by trigram French-likeness; none reaches the true key on any page. Independent Codex second transcription agrees 85.0-93.6% by value (lowest run per page).
Contributor: mechanical decode of every page and line-by-line conjectural readings of five letters (READING.en.md); most lines marked inferred (word division, supplied spelling, s/p choice).

Project re-measure (measure.py): contributed key re-applied by our own decoder; fr-1530-despatches LM -2.37 to -3.42 per char against -4.38 to -5.31 for the best of 200 shuffled keys per page (0 of 8,800 reach the true key); lexical coverage 81.0% of decoded letters in French words against 27.6% for shuffled keys and 90.3% for clean French.

Calibration on the contemporary decipherment (view 23 right), read here by eye: 1,000 of 1,193 letters (83.8%) of the decipherment matched by the contributed decode of view 22 right; 98 of 182 words of 3+ letters intact. A code group read SAXE where the decipherment has the duke of Wirtemberg; palatin missing.

Spot check on the Gallica images (views 22 and 99): view 22 right lines c01 and c03 compared sign by sign, 40/40 and 25 of 26 signs consistent with the contributed names, one not confirmed at this resolution; view 23 left found to carry about 17 further cipher lines of the 15 Nov 1567 letter, not in the contributed transcription.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): Harumi-Matsuba's per-page transcriptions and mechanical decodes (contributed/data/), the line-by-line readings of five letters (READING.en.md) and the contemporary decipherment of view 23 right (calib_v023r.txt); view 23 left (15 Nov 1567, second cipher page) is not transcribed

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): the 23 decoded_*.txt files are unspaced mechanical output (0-17% of sentences clean, docs/_check_reading.py) and READING.en.md was read through: f. 79r and f. 94r build into French sentences with scattered holes (kept read, reviewed B, those pages only); f. 39r-v, f. 100r and f. 158r have "..." holes in most lines. 21 letters relabelled decoded, not read; the two letters with a read first page kept read for that page. fraction_read 0.997 -> 0.056 (estimated).

Contact sheet of all 34 cipher views at reduced size (openapi.bnf.fr IIIF), then native crops of the margins: views 65, 103 and 125 right carry contemporary decipherments of their cipher in the left margin (65 not recorded before); view 37 right has a two-line margin decipherment; view 6 right holds an untranscribed first cipher page of the 11 Oct 1567 letter.

The rest of the contemporary decipherment on view 23 right (matching view 23 left) and the three margin decipherments (views 65, 103, 125 right) transcribed from native IIIF crops and aligned with the key decode; they agree clause by clause.

The other 19 letters built word by word into French from the key decode (decoded_*.txt), reading through the known sign confusions, with a few image checks (views 6, 37, 109, 159); translated. All 23 letters read (4 grade A, 19 B); docs/_check_reading.py clean share before 0.0-0.17 per page, after 0.50-1.0 per reading.

Sign values from the readings: a lone ϖ (and "pi") stands for l'Empereur (confirmed by the margins of views 65 and 103) or le Roy; 16 fits "vostre" in the 1569 letters to the King; H# = ss in ambassadeur/commissaires/asseurer, o elsewhere; =ii stands for a person (King of Spain, once the Landgrave). Not entered in key.tsv.
Phrase-level holes left open without image checks: 17 Jul 1568 f. 79v and f. 80, 4 Sep 1568 f. 100r c17-c27, 10 Sep 1569 v150l c17-c23, 15 Feb 1568 v038l c03-c04/c17-c18, 6 Mar 1568 f. 39r c22-c29.

Round 2 (23 Oct 2026): view 6 right, the untranscribed first cipher page of the 11 Oct 1567 letter, transcribed from native-resolution IIIF crops (23 lines, 816 signs, read/r2/transcription_v006r.txt) and read: the Emperor complains of the disorders in Christendom and blames the disunion of the Christian princes. Single AI transcription, 3.3% look-alike alternates; letter body score 0.61 plain, 0.92 holes only.

Round 2: the contributor's unvalued sign Dz (ꝺʒ) valued "con" (congé, conmandements, condition on view 6 right; conclusion, conditions, contanter, conservation in 1569; comme in 1568; consoler in Jul 1568): eleven words in five letters.

Round 2: view 23 left (15 Nov 1567) transcribed (13 lines, 446 signs, read/r2/transcription_v023l.txt) and decoded; with a re-reading of the contemporary decipherment on view 23 right it corrects three readings of 22 Oct ("il s'en va a Prague", "ceste lettre", "je n'ay eu responce"). Bearer's name and about 17 signs left open.

Round 2: 10 Sep 1569 view 150 left c14-c23 checked on native crops; label corrections (1 3y = code 18, "zo" = code 20) and Dz = con close the c17-c23 passage ("lesquelz il tient pour faictz", "de la conclusion", "quelques conditions", "pour cest effect, jusques au retour duquel"). Body score 0.54 -> 0.61; look-alike 3.0% without the y-shape class (4.1% upper bound). State decoded, not read -> read (B).

Round 2: phrase holes checked on native crops: 4 Sep 1568 f. 100r c16-c27 (mostly read; [pp] = King of Spain as mediator), 17 Jul 1568 f. 79v c06-c08 (read) and c01-c03, f. 80 c01/c08 (not settled), 15 Feb 1568 v038l c03-c04 (read) and c17-c18 (subject open), 6 Mar 1568 f. 39r c21-c29 (mostly read; ∞ code found).

r2m: the single-word holes of the 17 letters not re-checked in round 2 worked through on native-resolution openapi.bnf.fr IIIF crops (views 7, 8, 34, 35, 49, 65, 70, 71, 99, 100, 103, 109, 110, 125, 129, 130, 140, 141, 146, 155, 159, 161, 163, 168; scratchpad only) with the key and Dz = con. Bracketed holes in the 17 readings 161 -> 90 (view 6 right's, already checked in round 2, included). What closed them: number codes the contributed transcription read as letter signs (this hand writes 10 'ic', 13 'iz', 14 'i4', 18 'i8'/'ig', 20 'zo', 21 'zi', 23 'z3': e.g. 'jusques a tant', 'estre', 'est venue', 'vous'), the lone codes (the volume's ϖ for the Emperor or the King, pp for the King of Spain), Dz = con ('[con]me' x7, '[con]seiller'), groups the transcription left out (view 7 left c20 'sont [?soubz] les mains', view 110 right a whole line, cipher at the ends of clear lines on views 34 and 49), and words the 22 Oct readings had supplied that the figures contradict, now corrected: 'l'Emperatrice est venue' (not l'Empereur), 'l'evesque de Retes' (Bochetel, twice, not 'le sieur'), 'pourchassoict la seconde pour le roy de Portugal', 'poussoict ... le Turc', 'me faire ce bien de ne croire', 'car il ne sçavoict encores en quels termes', 'Et depuis' (the 'Il' of 20 Oct 1569 is the null 'Il ti ol'), 'Vanega' (Philip II's ambassador). Unsupported words withdrawn: 'arriver' (12 Jun 1568), '[?princes]' (20 Oct 1569), '[?Cosme]' (4 Sep 1568). Clean share (v2_score, plain / explicit holes) rises on 11 letters, e.g. 11 Oct 1567 0.461/0.724 -> 0.564/0.833, 20 Oct 1569 0.333/0.667 -> 0.400/0.867, 27 Mar 1568 0.385/0.846 -> 0.462/0.923; none falls below its state. The holes left give no word under the key or rest on a look-alike the figures do not settle (listed per letter in read/<doc>_reread_log.md, r2m sections; label corrections in read/r2/corrections.tsv).
Read bar applied per document (v10): 6 of 22 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Harumi-Matsuba's independent transcription and decode of view 23 left (issue #97; 445 signs, 13 lines) compared with ours of 23 Oct: same content; it settles the two open places as 'par le chemin de Flandres, par ce que c'est le plus court' (our 'le ...o...imin' = le chemin). Taken into read/1567-11-15_reading.md with doubt marks.

Second check (14 Nov 2026, Brice Dudout with Claude; NOTES): a separate decoder from contributed/data/key.tsv reproduces the contributor's decoded_*.txt on 45 pages, 32,272 of 32,352 letters (99.75%). The sign w, used 8 times, is missing from key.tsv: Tomokiyo's table has it as W in the double-letters row under r, so w = rr; the W shape seen on the Gallica images at 3 of the 8 places (view 70 right c04, c08; view 65 right c06), and the readings already read r there (courrier, conclure, verriez). fraction_read measured: 10,628 words read in the letters that read over 12,176 words and holes = 0.873 (was 0.91 estimated).

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's reconstructed key, published for the letters of this volume, applied by the contributor to their own transcription; the project re-applied it, calibrated one letter against the volume's contemporary decipherment (83.8% of letters), and on 22 Oct 2026 built every letter into French sentences from the decode; four letters (15 Nov 1567, 4 Jun, 21 Aug and 6 Nov 1568) follow contemporary decipherments found in the volume (view 23 right and the margins of views 65, 103 and 125 right).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Measured 14 Nov 2026 with research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.share on the 23 readings of outcome.texts: 11,615 words and 561 holes; the 22 letters that read hold 10,628 words read, so 10,628 / 12,176 = 0.873 (the 10 Sep 1569 letter, decoded, not read, counts as unread). The earlier estimate 0.91 was the letters' share of the words (measured 0.915) without the holes taken off. Earlier history: 22 Oct 2026, re-read (batch b02): all 23 letters build French sentences and are translated (read/<doc>_reading.md, _en.md; grades 4 A, 19 B). Signs of letters that read: the 29,707 transcribed signs, plus view 23 left (about 600 signs, untranscribed, read through its contemporary decipherment); not read: the first cipher page of the 11 Oct 1567 letter on view 6 right (about 800 signs, untranscribed). 30,300 / 31,100, so estimated. Holes remain inside the readings (Remaining gaps); docs/_check_reading.py clean share per reading 0.50-1.0 with header and notes counted. Earlier figures: 0.056 (audit, 22 Oct), 0.997 signs with a value (withdrawn as a reading figure). 23 Oct 2026 (round 2): every letter now reads, so every transcribed sign belongs to a letter that reads: 29,707 contributed signs + 816 (view 6 right, read/r2/transcription_v006r.txt) + 446 (view 23 left, read/r2/transcription_v023l.txt) = 30,969 of 30,969 (sign counts from the transcription files). Holes remain inside the readings (outcome.gaps); body clean share per reading 0.61-1.0 on docs/_check_reading.py's word list. Revised 23 Oct 2026 after round 2: 10 Sep 1569 kept decoded, not read on the look-alike limit; the letters that read hold about 91% of the reading files' words (estimated from word counts, not re-counted in signs).
outcome.notes: Contributed AI-only transcription (Claude + Codex), no human check. 22 Oct 2026: all 23 letters re-read into French sentences and translated (19 from the key decode, 4 after contemporary decipherments, three of them in margins not recorded before); class stays read in part: holes in several letters are workable by sign-level image checks, and the first cipher page of the 11 Oct 1567 letter (view 6 right) is untranscribed. 23 Oct 2026 (round 2): view 6 right and view 23 left transcribed and read, the 10 Sep 1569 letter now reads (all 23 letters read), Dz = con settled; class stays read in part: open codes and phrase holes remain inside the readings, and the transcription is AI-only with no human check.

texts.summary: Scipion de Fiesque, French envoy at the court of Emperor Maximilian II, to the Queen Mother, Vienna, Oct 1567 (date partly conjectural), during the negotiation of Charles IX's marriage with Elisabeth of Austria. Contents (conjectural, from the contributor's page list): The Emperor says he will do his utmost for peace in Christendom; The King's ambassador to Constantinople; The ambassador sent to Constantinople; marriages of the Emperor's daughters; Portugal; He will inquire, discreetly.
